Rekindling the Verdant Years Chapter 54: How a Good Class President is Made

On the athletic field, the boys from Class One would steal glances toward Ying Chanxi and Li Luo from time to time.

At first, their gazes were a little hostile. How could their class's prettiest girl be poached by a boy from another class?

But soon, a rumor spread.

It turned out that boy was Ying Chanxi's cousin.

During last night's dorm room chat, Liao Hailin had already talked about this in their room.

Now, with a few of his roommates spreading the word, the news quickly made its way through the boys' circle.

Li Luo was still completely oblivious to this. Squatting beside Ying Chanxi, he saw that she had nearly finished eating and patted his pants as he stood up, saying, "I'm going to go see Zhao Rongjun."

"Oh," Ying Chanxi nodded, then said, "I'll wait for you here for dinner. We can go to the cafeteria together later."

"Why do you always ask me to eat with you?"

"Can't a big sister supervise her little brother's diet to see if it's healthy?" Ying Chanxi pouted.

"I think a friendly meeting between the presidents of Class One and Class Eight has a bit more style."

"You're such a glib talker." Ying Chanxi shot him a look and waved her hand. "Go on, go on."

Watching Li Luo's departing figure, Qiao Xinyan sucked on the little pudding pop in her mouth, savoring this rare cool treat during military training. She couldn't help but say, "Your cousin is quite an interesting person. Are we eating dinner together later?"

"Umm..." Ying Chanxi glanced at Qiao Xinyan and suddenly fell into deep thought. "Xinyan, Li Luo is a pretty flighty guy. He's not as good as you say."

Qiao Xinyan looked at Ying Chanxi strangely. "He brought us drinks and pudding pops. How is that not good? It feels like your standards for your cousin are a bit high."

"Aiya... that's not what I mean..." Seeing that she was likely just praising Li Luo without any other intentions, Ying Chanxi's ears turned slightly red. "Then let's have dinner together later."

...

In Class Three's area.

Zhao Rongjun was sitting quietly on the ground, resting.

Just then, a tall girl walked over from the direction of the school store, carrying two bottles of iced water. She took one out and ambushed Zhao Rongjun from behind, pressing it against his face.

"Hiss..." Chilled by the ice, Zhao Rongjun instantly tilted his head back and glanced at the newcomer. "Luo Jiajia, you startled me."

"For you." Luo Jiajia, with her short hair, plopped down beside Zhao Rongjun in a carefree manner and handed over the water. "As thanks for the belt this morning."

"Thanks." Zhao Rongjun took the iced water, silently shifted over a bit, twisted the cap open, and took a sip. Then he said, "But I got that belt from a friend of mine."

"But you're the one who gave it to me," Luo Jiajia said. "I heard from others that buying one at the gate costs ten yuan, and the expensive ones are over ten or even twenty."

"...The friend who sells belts for ten yuan is me."

"Ah?" Luo Jiajia was stunned for a moment.

Just then, Li Luo's voice came from behind them. "I think I heard someone speaking ill of me."

Zhao Rongjun turned his head and immediately said, "Wasn't I just praising you?"

"Keep the belt-selling thing on the down-low." Li Luo squatted down, stuffed a little pudding pop into Zhao Rongjun's hands, and then looked at Luo Jiajia beside them. "Hello, I'm Li Luo from Class Eight."

"So you're the one selling belts at the gate?" Luo Jiajia blinked, asking curiously.

"My uncle sells them. It has nothing to do with me," Li Luo said as he pulled out another little pudding pop and handed it to Luo Jiajia. "Don't spread this around. Here's your hush money."

"Haha, I won't, I won't," Luo Jiajia said, taking the pudding pop. While eating, she asked, "But I think it's really impressive. Why can't you talk about it?"

"Who knows which school leader is connected to that clothing store at the gate," Li Luo pouted. "What I did was snatch food from the tiger's mouth. I made them lose out on several thousand yuan. I really don't want to be inexplicably targeted at school later on."

Of course, it was highly likely that the matter would just be dropped.

After all, selling belts was a once-a-year opportunity, and the clothing store owner wouldn't go to the trouble of making things difficult for a student like Li Luo.

Especially since she had earned quite a bit from Qianjiang University this year; it was just that Li Luo had intercepted her business at the First Affiliated High School.

But it was better to avoid trouble. Li Luo was past the age of actively showing off. He preferred his high school life to be peaceful and happy.

After chatting with Zhao Rongjun for a while, Li Luo patted his shoulder before leaving, giving him a suggestive look while glancing at Luo Jiajia out of the corner of his eye.

Seeing this, Zhao Rongjun looked completely exasperated and shook his head repeatedly, indicating that he had no interest in romance.

Li Luo sighed, not bothering with him. He patted his pants and walked back toward Class Eight.

At that moment, the homeroom teacher, Kong Junxiang, came downstairs to inspect. When he walked over to Class Eight, he saw three large boxes and asked out of curiosity, "What's this?"

"The class president had someone deliver drinks and ice cream," Hua Xiuxiu said, immediately reporting to Teacher Kong upon seeing him.

"Oh, is that so." Kong Junxiang glanced over. There were still leftover drinks and little pudding pops inside, and he felt a bit tempted.

But he was a teacher, after all, and was too embarrassed to take his students' things, so he just looked once before averting his gaze and asking Hua Xiuxiu about the military training.

If there was nothing major, he would head back to his office to enjoy the air conditioning and read his novels.

For these two days, the military training was still at school, so he could still enjoy himself. In a few days, when they went to the military barracks, he'd have to prepare to suffer.

"Teacher Kong." Li Luo walked back just then. Seeing Kong Junxiang, he strode forward, grabbed a bottle of soda and a little pudding pop. "Teacher, you're sweating. Have something to drink."

"Oh, thanks," Kong Junxiang said, accepting the drink and taking a reserved sip. "If there's nothing going on here, I'll be heading back."

"Okay, Teacher Kong." As Li Luo said this, he turned and put the remaining pudding pops from their box into the beverage box, then picked it up and followed Kong Junxiang.

"We still have some drinks and ice cream here. We won't be able to finish them when training starts in a bit, so I'll take them up and share them with the other teachers."

Kong Junxiang cast a surprised glance at Li Luo, then chuckled. "Alright, then I'll trouble you."

...

In the fifth-floor office, Li Luo quietly distributed the drinks and ice cream to the teachers, said goodbye to Kong Junxiang, and went back downstairs for military training.

After receiving the items, the teachers in the office all looked toward Kong Junxiang.

The English teacher, Teacher Ding, said with a smile, "What's up with Teacher Kong today? Treating us to drinks?"

"This isn't from me." Kong Junxiang took off his hat and placed it on his desk, saying with a cheerful smile, "That was our class president just now. He's the one who bought the drinks and ice cream."

"Hm? Your class president bought things and even thought of us?"

"He said he bought them for his classmates, and since they couldn't finish the leftovers, he brought them up."

"Do you believe that?" The math teacher, Teacher Li, glanced at Kong Junxiang. "Your class president is pretty good. He knows how to handle people."

"He's alright, just alright," Kong Junxiang said humbly. "He just gets things done in a way that saves me a lot of trouble."
